title: Telemetry spotlight miniroll playbook and wakeup notes
content:
Purpose: compact runbook for a small-cohort rollout (miniroll) that prioritizes telemetry sampling and fast rollback. Intended audience: release stewards, oncall, SRE, product owner. Status: working draft — lean, opinionated, intended as a 24–48h ops companion.

Quick summary / goals:
- Release window: 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-13 (night local) - 36h watch.
- Objective: validate a routing change + quantized model variant in prod with < 3% error-rate regression and < 15% p90 latency uplift.
- Safety net: automated fallback to previous routing tier + version pin if error budget crosses threshold.

Pre-launch checklist (T-72h to T-1h) — rapid items: 
- T-72h: confirm smoke images and load profile (Marco) — smoke tag: smoke/miniroll-0726
- T-48h: snapshot canary dashboards and set telemetry sampling to 100% for cohort (Liang)
- T-24h: dry-run traffic script against staging (Priya) — GitHub action: nightly/dryrun-serve
- T-4h: publish release notes draft in /customer-comms (link below) and pre-warn CS
- T-1h: flip safety gate to manual and confirm oncall pager + slack bridge: #release-watch

Launch hour cadence (hour-by-hour):
- +0m: open cohort at 0.5% of global traffic; annotate timeline in timeline doc
- +15m: quick smoke-checks (end-to-end): auth, rate-limit, streaming headers, small-kv cache hit sanity
- +30m: if green, increase to 3%; if any error spike > 1.5x baseline, rollback to 0% and notify TL
- +2h: expand to 10% if metrics stable, keep sampling at 100% for traces
- +8h: re-evaluate model-quality metrics (per-prompt eval set) and latency SLOs

Telemetry spotlight plan (how we sample & what to watch):
- Sampling: cohort requests + 100% trace sampling for first 8h, then 25% for next 24h.
- Signals: 1) 5xx error rate by route, 2) p50/p90/p99 latency by route & model-variant, 3) token-generation rate & aborts, 4) regression score on anchor eval set (anchor-id: AE-telemetry-0726), 5) memory pressure and GPU temperature anomalies.
- Alert thresholds (ops):
  - Alert A: 5xx rate > 0.8% sustained for 5m -> paging to release steward + SRE
  - Alert B: p90 latency > baseline * 1.2 for 15m -> slack notify then manual throttle
  - Alert C: regression score drop > 3% -> immediate soft-fail (throttle) and notify ML lead

Observability quick tasks (notes to SRE):
- Ensure KV cache TTLs are visible in per-route traces.
- Tag generated traces with cohort=miniroll-0726 and model_variant=quant-a2
- Pre-load a set of golden prompts as warm traces to prime cache before open

Rollback decision matrix (simple):
- Immediate rollback: any silent data corruption or loss (detected by parity checks), or regression > 5%
- Fast rollback: sustained error-rate above Alert A for > 15m OR latency > Alert B for 30m
- Graceful unwinding: non-critical quality regressions between 3–5% — pause expansion, A/B more sampling, schedule hotfix depending on root cause

Roles & comms (who does what):
- Release steward: Aisha (overall go/no-go)
- SRE lead oncall: Marco (pager responder, rollback exec)
- ML quality lead: Liang (assess anchor eval & regression signals)
- Product owner / CS liaise: Priya (customer-facing notes & CS brief)
- Ops runner: whoever is on deck — run the cadence checklist, mark timeline.

Release notes (draft for internal review):
- Title: "Miniroll: quant-a2 routing experiment — July 2026"
- Short: Gradual rollout of a quantized model variant behind routing rules to validate latency and cost improvements while verifying output quality on anchor prompts.
- Key changes: routing policy update to route 10% traffic to model quant-a2; added prefix caching for hot prompt families; telemetry sampling increased for cohort.
- Impact: expected token-cost reduction ~10–12% for cohort; potential p90 uplift < 15% (target); no expected customer-visible changes unless rollback occurs.
- Known issues: under certain long-context prompts the quantized path returns longer tail latency — being monitored.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Confirm whether autoscaler cooldown interacts with small-cohort burst noise (Marco to sim).
- Should we enable server-side deterministic seeds for anchor eval? pros/cons? (Liang)
- Draft customer-facing blurb once final metrics available (Priya)

Post-launch (T+8h to T+72h) runbook:
- T+8h: reduce trace sampling to 25% if no regressions, keep cohort at target percentage
- T+24h: run overnight regression sweep against anchor set and capture diff snapshots in GH PR
- T+48h: post-rollout retrospective notes (include line-level telemetry snapshots and short postmortem template if any threshold crossed)
- T+72h: final decision: promote change wider or roll back and open action items

Appendix: quick links & snippets
- Slack bridge: #release-watch (pinned docs)
- Staging dry-run action: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/actions/nightly/dryrun-serve
- Confluence baseline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/telemetry-baseline-2026
- Example smoke curl: curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DRYRUN' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Short journal entries (for operator to jot during launch):
- [ ] 00:00 cohort 0.5% open — smoke ok? yes/no — notes:
- [ ] 00:30 bump to 3% — errors? 
- [ ] 02:00 bump to 10% — latency shape?
- [ ] 08:00 regression sweep scheduled — snapshot id:

End of draft. This doc is intentionally terse — aim is to be used as a bedside playbook for the oncall and steward. Feedback welcome — drop comments inline or ping Aisha in slack.
